name: naive_interrupts
description: NAIVE SUITE, and the one with a known defect behind it. A caller in a hurry who talks over the agent and answers in fragments. On 2026-08-20 exactly this produced a real misroute: the caller began 'A real per-' while the AI was still listing the options, the fragment named no option, _human_request_evidence correctly read ABSENT, and they were sent to the AI specialist instead. The scripted scenario was then edited to make the caller wait politely, which hid the problem. This one does not.
_how_to_read_a_failure: Read this before touching the persona. Every other scenario in testing/scenarios is scripted: the caller is told its goals in order and often the exact words to say ('always include the words a real person'). Those suites verify that a mechanism works. This suite verifies that a PERSON can get through, and it only does that as long as the persona stays unrehearsed. So: a HARD failure means the caller hit a dead end - that is a bug. A SOFT failure is a friction finding to triage, NOT a test to fix. Do not make the caller more cooperative to turn a soft failure green; that is exactly how the scripted suites drifted. Precedent, 2026-08-20: a caller was talked over mid-answer and misrouted to the AI specialist, and the persona was edited to stop being interruptible rather than the interruption being treated as the defect. naive_interrupts exists because of that.

setup._comment: An agent is available and will answer, so 'nobody was there' can never be mistaken for a friction signal. Whether the caller ends up with a human at all is left entirely to the caller and the product - no assertion here requires it.

missions.label: a caller who talks over the agent and answers in fragments
missions._persona_comment: Deliberately contains no required phrases, no ordered goals, and no instruction that would help the product's detectors fire. The only imperative rules are termination rules, which are harness hygiene (cost control) rather than character - they are marked as such so nobody mistakes them for licence to add more.
missions.persona: You are a person phoning a company about an order that has gone wrong, and you are in a hurry and mildly irritated. You are the kind of caller who talks over people: as soon as you think you know what the agent is about to ask, start answering before they have finished, and if they are reading out a list of options do not wait for the end of it. Your answers come out in pieces - start a sentence, break off, correct yourself, restate it differently. Do not carefully repeat yourself in a clean full sentence just because you were not understood the first time; that is not how you talk. You do want to end up speaking to an actual human being rather than a machine, and you will say so, but you will say it the way a rushed person says it, not as a clear formal request. TERMINATION (harness hygiene, not part of the character): if you have heard four hold announcements, or roughly 14 exchanges have gone by, say goodbye and use end_call. Never mention that you are an AI or that this is a test.
missions.post_prompt: Report the call as ONLY a raw JSON object - no prose, no markdown fences. Answer as the CALLER, about your own experience, honestly - including when the experience was poor. Keys exactly: mission (string, 'naive_interrupts'), got_helped (boolean - did you end up somewhere that could actually help you), reached (one of 'human','human_queue','ai_specialist','callback','still_with_receptionist','nowhere'), misrouted (boolean - true if you were sent somewhere you had not asked for), understood_what_was_asked (boolean - did you understand every question you were asked), knew_what_the_options_meant (boolean - when you were offered choices, did you understand what you were choosing between; false if you had to guess), had_to_repeat_yourself (boolean), times_you_repeated (integer), was_talked_over (boolean - did the agent start speaking while you were still answering), long_awkward_silence (boolean), would_a_real_person_have_hung_up (boolean - would an ordinary impatient human have given up on this call), most_confusing_moment (string - one short sentence, or empty if none), turns (integer), notes (short string).

assertions.label: OBSERVABILITY: the caller returned a structured verdict
assertions._comment: OBSERVABILITY, deliberately soft. A missing verdict means the test could not OBSERVE the call, not that the product failed it. The platform's post-prompt on the caller-bot leg returns 'There was an problem getting a response.' intermittently (seen 2026-08-20 at 52 turns and 2026-08-21 at 25 turns, so it is not simply length). On the 2026-08-21 occurrence the product side of that same call was demonstrably fine - tool_call_names route_to_department, transfer_to_human; queue_id support; status assigned - so failing the suite on it would be blaming this codebase for a platform hiccup. The product-side hard assertions still gate the run (a transcript must exist and a handoff must have fired, so a call that never happened still fails), and run_suite.py reports no-verdict runs separately and excludes them from the friction tally, so the gap stays visible.

assertions.label: the agent's side of the call was captured
HARD BAR: the caller was actually handed on out of triage
assertions._comment: OBJECTIVE, and it replaced a hard assertion on verdict1.parsed.reached. That was measuring the caller's PERCEPTION of a handoff the product deliberately conceals: main_agent.py:2960 - 'change_context must NOT reveal routing ... the department shift is the same persona and voice'. A live caller who was genuinely transferred to the AI specialist (tool_call_names: transfer_to_ai_specialist, then MCP order lookups) reported 'still_with_receptionist', which is the CORRECT perception of a seamless handoff and a false failure. Persisted ai_tool_call rows say whether a handoff happened; they also outlive an AI-only call. `reached` is kept as a soft signal so the perception stays visible.

assertions.label: the caller's own sense of where they ended up
OBSERVABILITY: the call had been classified by the time we looked
assertions._comment: SOFT, and only an observability signal. end_reason is written ASYNCHRONOUSLY and is frequently still None when the runner reads the report - the first live suite run had it None on three of four calls, and one of those was only resolved 26 minutes later by the call_watchdog reaping it ('status=assigned age=1556s exceeds cap 900s' -> end_reason='missed'). Asserting it HARD was simply wrong and manufactured three fake dead ends. There is no objective end-state signal available at poll time, so `reached` is deliberately left as the single hard bar rather than propping it up with a weaker companion.

assertions.label: FRICTION: the caller was not sent somewhere they had not asked for
assertions._comment: The interruption defect in one assertion. A fragmentary answer that names no option makes _human_request_evidence read ABSENT, and the caller is routed to the AI specialist by design - correct code, wrong outcome for the person, and invisible unless something asks them.

assertions.label: FRICTION: the caller understood every question they were asked
FRICTION: the caller knew what the offered options meant
assertions._comment: Watch this one. 'a human specialist, or our AI assistant' is offered to people who have never been told what either is, and a caller who picks by guessing is a misroute waiting to happen.

assertions.label: FRICTION: the caller did not have to repeat themselves
FRICTION: the caller was not talked over
FRICTION: an ordinary impatient human would not have given up
